statement:
Let $F/\mathbb{Q}$ be a Galois extension and let $\rho$ be an irreducible Artin representation factoring through $F/\mathbb{Q}$. Write $\langle\rho,E(F)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb C\rangle$ for its multiplicity, and let $w(E/\mathbb Q,\rho)$ be the corresponding twisted global root number.

**Minimalist conjecture for twists.** For $100\%$ of elliptic curves $E/\mathbb Q$,

$$
\langle \rho,E(F)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb C\rangle=
\begin{cases}
0 & \text{if }\rho\text{ is not self-dual},\\
0 & \text{if }w(E/\mathbb Q,\rho)=+1,\\
1 & \text{if }w(E/\mathbb Q,\rho)=-1.
\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture predicts the smallest possible multiplicity compatible with the parity conjecture for twists, for almost all elliptic curves in the stated ordering. It is presented as folklore and remains open.
title: The minimalist conjecture for elliptic-curve Artin twists
source_name: Lilybelle Cowland Kellock and Vladimir Dokchitser, “Root numbers and parity phenomena”, arXiv:2303.07883 (2023).
technical_reason: Density-one multiplicity over all elliptic curves includes rank-distribution obstacles even for trivial rho; no bounded full-scope route. Parity alone is insufficient.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. Its arboricity $\operatorname{arb}(G)$ is the least number of colors in an edge coloring with no monochromatic cycle, and its strong arboricity $\zeta(G)$ is the least number of colors in a coloring that remains acyclic after contracting any single edge. The girth of $G$ is the length of its shortest cycle.

**Large-girth strong arboricity conjecture.** For every integer $k$ there is an integer $g(k)$ such that every graph $G$ with

$$
\operatorname{arb}(G)\leqslant k
$$

and girth at least $g(k)$ satisfies

$$
\zeta(G)=\operatorname{arb}(G).
$$

The conjecture expresses the expectation that sufficiently large girth makes strong arboricity attain its smallest possible value, namely arboricity, within every bounded-arboricity class.
title: Large-girth strong arboricity conjecture
source_name: Tomasz Bartnicki, Sebastian Czerwiński, Jarosław Grytczuk and Zofia Miechowicz, “Strong arboricity of graphs”, arXiv:2303.08771 (2023).
technical_reason: Requires a uniform girth threshold for every bounded arboricity, not a finite high-girth example; no recoloring invariant ensuring every contraction was found.

statement:
Fix an integer $n\geq 3$ and a parameter $\alpha\in(0,1)$. Let $T_\alpha$ be the corresponding continued fraction transformation, let $\mu$ be the invariant measure on its natural-extension domain $\Omega_\alpha$, and let $\operatorname{vol}_n$ denote the volume of the unit tangent bundle of the hyperbolic orbifold uniformized by the triangle group $G_n$:

$$
\operatorname{vol}_n=\frac{2(2n-3)\pi^2}{3n}.
$$

**Entropy-volume conjecture.** For all $n\geq 3$ and all $\alpha\in(0,1)$,

$$
h(T_\alpha)\,\mu(\Omega_\alpha)=\operatorname{vol}_n.
$$

The identity is equivalent in the paper to the conjectured geometric realization of the first pointwise expansive power as a geodesic-flow return map. It is proved on certain parameter intervals and numerically confirmed for $4\leq n\leq 12$, but remains conjectural in full generality.
title: Entropy-volume conjecture for triangle-group continued fraction transformations
source_name: Kariane Calta, Cor Kraaikamp and Thomas A. Schmidt, “Continuity of entropy for all α-deformations of an infinite class of continued fraction transformations”, arXiv:2303.09708 (2023).
technical_reason: All n and real alpha require natural-extension measure and return-time identities; checking finitely many n or continuity does not establish the common product.

statement:
Let $C_{2\ell}^{\square}=C_{2\ell}\square K_2$ be the $2\ell$-prism, formed from two vertex-disjoint $2\ell$-cycles with a matching joining corresponding vertices. For a graph $H$, let $\mathrm{ex}(n,H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $H$-free graph. **He–Li–Feng's even-prism conjecture.** For every $\ell\ge 2$, there exists $c=c(\ell)>0$ such that

$$
\mathrm{ex}(n,C_{2\ell}^{\square})=O(n^{5/3-c}).
$$

The conjecture seeks to improve the general dependent-random-choice upper bound beyond the exponent $5/3$. It is solved for every $\ell\ge 4$, where the extremal number is in fact $\Theta_{\ell}(n^{3/2})$; the case $\ell=3$ remains weaker in the paper's discussion.
title: He–Li–Feng's even-prism extremal-number conjecture
source_name: Jun Gao, Oliver Janzer, Hong Liu and Zixiang Xu, “Extremal number of graphs from geometric shapes”, arXiv:2303.13380 (2023).
technical_reason: All ell includes cube ell=2 and ell=3; ell>=4 theorem does not finish scope. Corpus reference about unrelated cubic bipartite H is not evidence of a prism refutation.

statement:
Let $S=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, let $J_{n,m}$ be the path ideal of the cycle graph on $n$ vertices with paths of length $m$, let $d$ be the parameter defined by the paper for $n$ and $m$, and let $t\geq 1$. **Depth conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{depth}(S/J_{n,m}^t)\geq d-1.
$$

The preceding theorem establishes the corresponding upper bound for all $t\geq t_0$, so the conjecture would determine the depth as $d-1$ for those powers. It is proposed on the basis of computer experiments in CoCoA; the general lower bound for all powers remains open.
title: Depth lower bound for powers of the path ideal of a cycle graph
source_name: Silviu Balanescu and Mircea Cimpoeas, “Depth and Stanley depth of powers of the path ideal of a cycle graph”, arXiv:2303.15032 (2024).
technical_reason: Parameter d and path-length convention need primary definitions; an arbitrary-power depth lower bound requires homological machinery beyond a small monomial certificate.

statement:
Let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be positive integers. Write $d=\gcd(m_1,m_2)$, and let $2^s$ be the largest power of $2$ dividing both $m_1$ and $m_2$. For a sufficiently large integer $n$, impose

$$
\gcd(n,m_1)=\gcd(n,m_2)=d,
$$

and

$$
n\equiv m_1+m_2\pmod{2^{s+1}}.
$$

**Generalised Goldbach conjecture.** Under these conditions, there exist primes $p$ and $q$ such that

$$
n=m_1p+m_2q.
$$

This conjecture includes the even Goldbach conjecture when $(m_1,m_2)=(1,1)$ and Lemoine's conjecture when $(m_1,m_2)=(1,2)$. Its general proof is stated to be out of reach; the paper empirically tests instances for coefficients up to $40$.
title: The generalised Goldbach conjecture for weighted prime sums
source_name: Zsófia Juhász, Máté Bartalos, Péter Magyar and Gábor Farkas, “Empirical verification of a new generalisation of Goldbach's conjecture up to 10^12 (or 10^13) for all coefficients 40”, arXiv:2304.00024 (2023).
technical_reason: Coefficient pair (1,1) contains asymptotic binary Goldbach; finite prime sweeps cannot establish sufficiently-large quantifier.

statement: Let $f_2(n)$ be the minimum number of arcs in an oriented graph with weak diameter $2$ on $n$ vertices. An **oriented clique** is an oriented graph in which every pair of distinct vertices is joined by a directed path of length at most $2$ in one direction, and a **cut vertex** is a vertex whose removal disconnects the underlying graph. **Cut-vertex extremal conjecture.** For all $n>5$, there exists an oriented clique with $n$ vertices having a cut vertex. This is the second conjectural ingredient proposed together with the maximum-degree statement; the supplied text gives no proof or resolution.
title: The cut-vertex extremal oriented clique conjecture
source_name: Sandip Das, Koushik Kumar Dey, Pavan P D and Sagnik Sen, “Counting the minimum number of arcs in an oriented graph having weak diameter 2”, arXiv:2304.00742 (2024).
technical_reason: Primary v2 Conjecture 6.1 requires exactly f_2(n) arcs, omitted from record. A singleton -> cut vertex -> transitive tournament construction proves literal existence routinely but does not prove extremal conjecture; no credit.
local_proof: No new candidate proof; rejected wording diagnostics only

statement:
For a positive integer $d$, let $Z(d)$ denote the relevant extremal matching-number threshold, and let $f_{\Delta}(d,m)$ be the maximum number of edges in a triangle-free graph with matching number $m$ and maximum degree bounded in the setting of the source. For natural numbers $d\geq 2$ and $m$, write

$$
m=kZ(d)+r.
$$

**Ahanjideh–Ekim–Yıldız conjecture.** For all natural numbers $d\geq 2$ and $m$, we have

$$
f_{\Delta}(d,m)=\begin{cases} dm+k\left\lfloor d/2\right\rfloor,&\text{if }r<d,\\ dm+k\left\lfloor d/2\right\rfloor+r-d+1,&\text{if }r\geq d.\end{cases}
$$

This formula extends the cases established in the source to the remaining open cases and would give the general edge-extremal function for the considered class of triangle-free graphs.
title: Ahanjideh–Ekim–Yıldız formula for maximum edges in triangle-free graphs
source_name: Ali Erdem Banak, Tınaz Ekim and Z. Caner Taşkın, “Constructing extremal triangle-free graphs using integer programming”, arXiv:2304.01729 (2023).
technical_reason: Z(d) and admissible graph constraints require source definitions; a piecewise formula for every d,m needs extremal upper bounds, not isolated integer-programming optima.

statement:
Let $\mathbb{P}_g^{\mathrm{\scriptsize{WP}}}$ denote the Weil–Petersson probability measure on compact hyperbolic surfaces of genus $g$, and let $\lambda_1>0$ be the smallest non-zero eigenvalue of their positive Laplace–Beltrami operator. **Typical near-optimal spectral gap conjecture.** For any $\epsilon>0$, 

$$
\lim_{g\rightarrow +\infty}\mathbb{P}_g^{\mathrm{\scriptsize{WP}}}\left(\lambda_1\geq\frac14-\epsilon\right)=1.
$$

This conjectures that a near-optimal spectral gap is typical for large-genus Weil–Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces, strengthening the previously known probabilistic lower bounds $3/16-\epsilon$ and the theorem giving $2/9-\epsilon$.
title: Typical near-optimal spectral gap conjecture for Weil–Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces
source_name: Nalini Anantharaman and Laura Monk, “Friedman-Ramanujan functions in random hyperbolic geometry and application to spectral gaps I”, arXiv:2304.02678 (2026).
technical_reason: Near-1/4 high-genus probability limit requires uniform geometric spectral analysis. No small certificate; possible public resolution unverified, not cleared.

statement:
Let ${\rm ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,2C_4)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex planar graph containing no two vertex-disjoint copies of $C_4$. **Li's conjecture.** If $n\geq 23$, then

$$
{\rm ex}_{\mathcal{P}}(n,2C_4)\leq \frac{19}{7}(n-2),
$$

and this bound is tight whenever $14\mid(n-2)$. This conjecture proposes the exact linear upper bound, together with an infinite family of values of $n$ for which equality is attained; its status is not resolved by the supplied source.
title: Li's planar Turán conjecture for two 4-cycles
source_name: Longfei Fang, Huiqiu Lin and Yongtang Shi, “Extremal spectral results of planar graphs without vertex-disjoint cycles”, arXiv:2304.06942 (2023).
technical_reason: Exact planar edge bound plus infinitely many sharpness values requires structural charging and constructions; Euler bound 3n-6 is too weak.

statement:
Let $n\geq4$ and let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph with minimum degree $\delta(G)>\frac{3}{4}n$. A **2-edge-coloring** of $G$ is a partition $E(G)=E(B)\uplus E(R)$ into blue and red edges. **Li, Nikiforov and Schelp's conjecture.** Every such coloring has a color containing every cycle length $k$ with $4\leq k\leq\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil$; that is, either

$$
C_k\subseteq E(B)\quad\text{for all }k\in[4,\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil]
$$

or

$$
C_k\subseteq E(R)\quad\text{for all }k\in[4,\lceil\frac{n}{2}\rceil].
$$

The conjecture is known for sufficiently large $n$ and $k\in[4,(\frac18-o(1))n]$, while the full assertion remains open.
title: Li, Nikiforov and Schelp's monochromatic cycle conjecture
source_name: Yiran Zhang and Yuejian Peng, “Monochromatic cycles in 2-edge-colored bipartite graphs with large minimum degree”, arXiv:2304.08003 (2024).
technical_reason: Same color must contain every requested length. Separate colors per length or asymptotic subinterval results do not meet quantifier; no bounded route.

statement:
Let

$$
\mathcal{R}=\{a\in\mathbb{N}_{+}:\text{ the curve }y^2=x^3+ax\text{ has positive rank}\}.
$$

For $a\in\mathcal{R}$, define

$$
m(a)=\min\{Q\in\mathbb{N}_{\geq2}:(a,Q)\text{ is a proper solution of the paper's problem}\}.
$$

A positive integer is **fourth power-free** if it is not divisible by the fourth power of any prime. **Well-definedness conjecture.** The function $m:\mathcal{R}\to\{Q\in\mathbb{N}_{+}:Q\text{ is fourth power-free}\}$ is well defined. This asserts that the minimum exists for every $a\in\mathcal{R}$ and always has the stated fourth-power-free property; computations verify existence in the reported range $a\leq10^4$.
title: Well-definedness conjecture for the minimal quotient function
source_name: Maciej Ulas, “Geometric progressions in the sets of values of rational functions”, arXiv:2304.09264 (2023).
technical_reason: Proper solution is undefined in record and must be recovered before using positive rank to force a minimum and fourth-power-free condition; no eligible route.

statement:
Let $k$ be a finite field, let $n\geq 6$, and write $h(\operatorname{GL}_n(k))$ for the Harada invariant of the finite general linear group. Let $v_q(h(\operatorname{GL}_n(k)))$ denote the polynomial in the field order $q$ obtained in the paper.

**Root bound conjecture.** For $n\geq 6$, the maximum real root of $v_q(h(\operatorname{GL}_n(k)))$ is less than $2$.

The bound would imply that $h(\operatorname{GL}_n(k))$ is integral for every finite field with $q\geq 2$, extending the verified cases $2\leq n\leq 5$ and the theorem for sufficiently large $q$.
title: Conjecture on the roots of the Harada invariant for general linear groups
source_name: Masahiro Sugimoto, “Harada's conjecture II for the finite general linear groups and unitary groups”, arXiv:2304.10708 (2024).
technical_reason: Root bound concerns a polynomial in field-order variable for every n>=6; integrality at actual prime powers is weaker. Polynomial coefficients not primary-verified.

statement: For each integer $n\geq2$, let $V/G$ be the quotient of the hypersurface constructed in the paper by the cyclic group action described there; it is a klt Calabi–Yau variety of dimension $n$ with minimal log discrepancy $1/m$. **Minimal mld conjecture for varieties.** For every $n\geq2$, the quotient $V/G$ has the smallest minimal log discrepancy among all klt Calabi–Yau varieties of dimension $n$. The construction gives minimal log discrepancies that decay doubly exponentially with dimension and are close to the conjecturally optimal values for pairs, providing evidence for the conjecture; the source does not state that it has been resolved.
title: Minimal mld conjecture for the constructed klt Calabi–Yau varieties
source_name: Louis Esser, “Minimal log discrepancies of hypersurface mirrors”, arXiv:2304.13823 (2024).
technical_reason: Optimal minimal discrepancy among all klt Calabi-Yau varieties needs global birational bounds; the explicit quotient alone is no optimality proof.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with average vertex degree at most $k$, where $k\geq 1$. Let $i(G)$ denote the independent domination number of $G$, and let $\partial_k(G)$ denote the minimum number of vertices in a $k$-dominating set of $G$. **Average-degree domination conjecture.** For every such graph $G$, the inequality

$$
i(G)\geq \partial_k(G)
$$

holds. Moreover, equality occurs if and only if $G$ is $k$-regular.

This conjecture generalizes the paper's theorem for outerplanar graphs, which asserts the strict inequality $i(G)>\partial_4(G)$. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
title: The average-degree generalization of the independent-set domination inequality
source_name: Dmitrii Taletskii, “Independent sets versus 4-dominating sets in outerplanar graphs”, arXiv:2305.01577 (2023).
technical_reason: Average degree does not control local k-domination and the convention for partial_k needs primary checking. No credit for apparent convention reversal or regularity endpoint.

statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph, let $k$ be a positive integer, and write $\delta^{+}(D)$ for its minimum out-degree. A **transitive tournament** on $k$ vertices is the tournament whose vertices admit an ordering in which every edge points forward; an immersion replaces its directed edges by pairwise edge-disjoint directed paths. **Linear out-degree immersion conjecture.** There exists an absolute constant $C>0$ such that, for every positive integer $k$, every digraph $D$ satisfying

$$
\delta^{+}(D)\geq Ck
$$

contains an immersion of a transitive tournament on $k$ vertices. Lochet proved the analogous assertion with an unspecified function of $k$, while the linear bound for arbitrary digraphs remains open.
title: Linear minimum-out-degree conjecture for transitive tournament immersions
source_name: António Girão and Robert Hancock, “Immersions of directed graphs in tournaments”, arXiv:2305.06204 (2024).
technical_reason: Linear constant must work for every k and digraph. Bounded tournament immersions or an unspecified function do not yield a linear route.

statement:
Let $\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{H}}(n,C_6)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex Halin graph containing no cycle of length $6$. **The sharp upper-bound conjecture.** For $n\geq 21$, 

$$
\operatorname{ex}_{\mathcal{H}}(n,C_6)\leq \frac{8}{5}(n-1).
$$

This conjecture proposes the sharp upper bound for the Halin Turán number of the $6$-cycle; its status is not established by the supplied source context.
title: The sharp upper-bound conjecture for the Halin Turán number of the 6-cycle
source_name: Addisu Paulos, “On the Halin Turán number of short cycles”, arXiv:2305.08331 (2023).
technical_reason: Halin C6-free bound for every n>=21 suggests finite-state tree-face analysis, but no proved reduction to a bounded state set or full-scope certificate available.

statement:
Fix $N>2$ and $d\geq 1$. Let $\Omega_N$ be the group of $N$th roots of unity, and let $f:\Omega_N^n\to\mathbf{C}$ have degree at most $d$ and local degree at most $N-1$, so that

$$
f(z)=\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,1,\dots,N-1\}^n:\lvert\alpha\rvert\leq d}a_{\alpha}z^{\alpha}.
$$

**Generalized Maximum Modulus Principle.** There exists $C(d,N)>0$, independent of $n$, such that for every $n\geq 1$,

$$
\max_{z\in\operatorname{conv}(\Omega_N)^n}\lvert f(z)\rvert\leq C(d,N)\max_{z\in\Omega_N^n}\lvert f(z)\rvert.
$$

For $N=\infty$ and $N=2$ the analogous inequality is trivial with constant $1$, whereas the case $2<N<\infty$ is described as highly non-trivial and motivates the conjecture.
title: Generalized Maximum Modulus Principle for cyclic groups
source_name: Joseph Slote, Alexander Volberg and Haonan Zhang, “Bohnenblust–Hille inequality for cyclic groups”, arXiv:2305.10560 (2024).
technical_reason: Primary 2305.10560v4 explicitly reports solution. Actual successor 2305.10828v3 Theorem 1 bounds the torus for all K>=2,d,n; maximum modulus on the polydisc implies the weaker convex-hull bound. 2310.07926v6 Theorem 1 gives an even stronger disc theorem. Selected proof bodies read, dependencies not fully audited.

statement:
For each positive integer $k$, let $\alpha_k$ be the minimum value such that there is a constant $c_k$ with

$$
\omega(G^2)\leqslant \alpha_kD+c_k
$$

whenever $G$ is $k$-degenerate and has maximum degree at most $D$. Let $\beta_k$ be the minimum value such that there is a constant $d_k$ with

$$
\omega(G^2)\leqslant \beta_kD+d_k
$$

whenever $G$ has maximum average degree less than $2k$ and maximum degree at most $D$. The **equality conjecture** states that, for all $k\geqslant 2$,

$$
\beta_k=\alpha_k.
$$

The paper proves the equality for $k=2$, while its validity for larger values of $k$ remains open; the authors do not conjecture the precise values of either parameter.
title: Equality of the asymptotic clique bounds for bounded maximum average degree
source_name: Daniel W. Cranston and Gexin Yu, “Cliques in Squares of Graphs with Maximum Average Degree less than 4”, arXiv:2305.11763 (2024).
technical_reason: Equality of two optimum asymptotic constants for every k>=2 cannot follow from the inclusion of the mad class into k-degenerate graphs in the needed reverse direction; no extremal-transfer construction found.

statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a class of graphs of bounded stretch-width. For an $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal C$, let the **clique-width** of $G$ be the minimum number of labels needed to construct $G$ using the clique-width operations. **Logarithmic clique-width conjecture.** There is a constant $c$ such that for every $n$-vertex graph $G\in\mathcal C$, the clique-width of $G$ is at most $c\log n$. This would clarify whether bounded stretch-width generally implies essentially logarithmic clique-width; the paper provides a separating example with essentially logarithmic clique-width, but the general statement is posed as an open question.
title: Logarithmic clique-width conjecture for classes of bounded stretch-width
source_name: Édouard Bonnet and Julien Duron, “Stretch-width”, arXiv:2305.12023 (2023).
technical_reason: Uniform logarithmic clique-width requires a construction from bounded stretch-width for every graph; one separating example proves neither direction of the universal upper bound.

statement:
A **tournament** is an orientation of a complete graph. For non-negative integers $l$ and $k$, an $l$-flash is a directed walk of length $l$ whose edge colours are all the same, and a $k$-rainbow is a directed walk of length $k$ whose edge colours are all distinct. Let $t(l,k)$ be the smallest integer such that every edge-colouring of every tournament with more than $t(l,k)$ vertices contains an $l$-flash or a $k$-rainbow. **Tournament strengthening.** For all positive integers $l$ and $k$, 
$$
t(l,k)=l^{k-1}.
$$
 This extends the transitive-tournament problem defining $f(l,k)$; the source states that it remains wide open for every $l\geqslant 2$ and $k\geqslant 3$.
title: Tournament strengthening of the Lefmann–Rödl–Thomas conjecture
source_name: António Girão, Freddie Illingworth, Lukas Michel, Michael Savery and Alex Scott, “Flashes and rainbows in tournaments”, arXiv:2305.13422 (2023).
technical_reason: All tournament edge-colorings require controlling arbitrary repeated-color walks; transitive cases and k=2 do not establish general exact l^(k-1).

statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power and let $k$ and $n$ be positive integers satisfying $n>2k$. A cyclic subspace code is a single-orbit code under scalar multiplication, and $\mathcal{G}_q(n,k)$ denotes the Grassmannian of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$.

**Existence conjecture.** There exists a cyclic subspace code $\mathcal{C}\subseteq \mathcal{G}_q(n,k)$ such that

$$
|\mathcal{C}|=\frac{q^n-1}{q-1}
$$

and

$$
d(\mathcal{C})=2k-2.
$$

Such codes would attain the stated orbit size and minimum distance simultaneously for every prime power $q$ and all positive integers $k,n$ with $n>2k$.
title: Existence of optimal cyclic subspace codes
source_name: Yun Li, Hongwei Liu and Sihem Mesnager, “Constructions of Constant Dimension Subspace Codes”, arXiv:2305.13913 (2023).
technical_reason: Uniform full orbit and exact distance require Sidon-space type constructions in every field extension. k=1 distance convention is only a wording issue, not substantive refutation.

statement:
Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, with minimum degree $\delta(G)$ and independence number $\alpha(G)$. A **square of a Hamilton cycle** is the graph obtained by joining vertices whose distance on the Hamilton cycle is at most two.

**Staden–Treglown conjecture.** For every $\mu>0$, there exist $\alpha>0$ and $
_0\in \mathbb{N}$ such that the following holds. For every $n$-vertex graph $G$ with $
\geq n_0$, if

$$
\delta(G)\geq \left(\frac{1}{2}+\mu\right)n
$$

and

$$
\alpha(G)\leq \alpha n,
$$

then $G$ contains a square of a Hamilton cycle.

This conjecture concerns Hamiltonian spanning structures in graphs with sublinear independence number. The source attributes it to Staden and Treglown; its resolution status is not specified here.
title: Staden–Treglown conjecture for squares of Hamilton cycles
source_name: Ming Chen, Jie Han, Yantao Tang and Donglei Yang, “On powers of Hamilton cycles in Ramsey-Turán Theory”, arXiv:2305.17360 (2023).
technical_reason: Asymptotic spanning square under sparse independence needs an absorption/regularity chain; malformed n_0 text retained literally. No short full-scope route.

statement:
For every set of points $P\subset[0,1]^2$, let $\Phi(P)$ be the smallest real number $w\geqslant0$ for which some strip of width $w$ contains at least three points of $P$. Define

$$
\Phi(n):=\max\Phi(P),
$$

where the maximum is over all sets of $n$ points $P\subset[0,1]^2$. **Motzkin–Schmidt conjecture.** The maximum strip width satisfies

$$
\Phi(n)=o(1/n).
$$

A simple pigeonholing argument gives $\Phi(n)\leqslant3/n$, and Beck proved the conjecture for uniformly distributed point sets, but no nontrivial upper bound is known in general. The conjecture is directly related to the Heilbronn triangle problem through $\Delta(n)\leqslant\Phi(n)$, although the converse implication need not hold.
title: Motzkin–Schmidt strip-width conjecture
source_name: Alex Cohen, Cosmin Pohoata and Dmitrii Zakharov, “A new upper bound for the Heilbronn triangle problem”, arXiv:2305.18253 (2023).
technical_reason: Little-o requires improvement for arbitrary point sets uniformly in n; numerical configurations or uniformly distributed special case do not imply it.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta_G\leq D$. Let $\Gamma$ be an arbitrary color set, let $S_v\subseteq\Gamma$ satisfy $|S_v|=D+1$ for every vertex $v$, and let each $L_v$ be a uniformly random $\ell$-subset of $S_v$, where

$$
\ell=(1+\varepsilon)\log n
$$

for fixed $\varepsilon>0$.

**Palette-sparsification conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $L$-colorable with high probability.

This is presented as an expected extension of the paper's main theorem and of the Alon–Assadi framework. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
title: Palette-sparsification conjecture for arbitrary palettes
source_name: Jeff Kahn and Charles Kenney, “Asymptotics for Palette Sparsification”, arXiv:2306.00171 (2023).
technical_reason: Global arbitrary palettes require high-probability coloring at logarithmic list size; nonintegral ell and ell>D+1 need standard convention, not a discovery. No uniform dependency argument.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on vertex set $V$ with degree $d_v$ at each vertex $v$. Let $\Gamma$ be an arbitrary color set, let $S_v\subseteq\Gamma$ satisfy $|S_v|=d_v+1$ for every $v\in V$, and let each $L_v$ be a uniformly random $\ell$-subset of $S_v$, where

$$
\ell=(1+\varepsilon)\log n
$$

for fixed $\varepsilon>0$.

**Local palette-sparsification conjecture.** The graph $G$ is $L$-colorable with high probability.

The source describes this as a further suspected extension that removes the global maximum-degree palette size and uses the natural local threshold. No resolution is given, so it remains open.
title: Palette-sparsification conjecture at the local degree threshold
source_name: Jeff Kahn and Charles Kenney, “Asymptotics for Palette Sparsification”, arXiv:2306.00171 (2023).
technical_reason: Local palettes d_v+1 add low-degree truncation issues; endpoint list-size corrections earn no credit and no probabilistic full-scope mechanism is established.

statement:
For graphs $G$ and $H$, the Ramsey number $r(G,H)$ is the smallest positive integer $N$ such that every red/blue edge-coloring of the complete graph $K_N$ contains either a red $G$ or a blue $H$. A book $B_n$ is a graph consisting of $n$ triangles sharing a common edge. **Conlon–Fox–Wigderson's conjecture.** For every $\alpha<1$, the random lower bound for $r(B_{\alpha n},B_n)$ is not tight. In other words, there exists some $\beta=\beta(\alpha)>0$ such that

$$
r(B_{\alpha n},B_n)\ge (\sqrt{\alpha}+1)^2n+\beta n
$$

for all $n$ sufficiently large. The conjecture predicts a linear improvement over the random lower bound in the unbalanced book Ramsey problem; its resolution is not established in the supplied source.
title: Conlon–Fox–Wigderson's book Ramsey-number conjecture
source_name: Chunchao Fan, Qizhong Lin and Yuanhui Yan, “On a conjecture of Conlon, Fox and Wigderson”, arXiv:2306.05054 (2024).
technical_reason: For every 0<alpha<1 requires a strict linear improvement on random bound, with beta depending on alpha. A few explicit colorings cannot cover continuum of ratios.

statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, finite or infinite. For each edge $e\in E(G)$, let $L(e)$ be a list of available colours. The list distinguishing index $D'_l(G)$ is the minimum cardinal number $k$ such that every assignment of lists of cardinality $k$ admits a distinguishing edge colouring $c$ with $c(e)\in L(e)$ for every edge $e\in E(G)$. The distinguishing index $D'(G)$ is the minimum number of colours in a distinguishing edge colouring of $G$.

**List distinguishing index conjecture.**

$$
D'_l(G)=D'(G).
$$

This conjecture extends the finite-graph vertex list-distinguishing conjecture to edge colourings and to connected infinite graphs. The source presents it as being motivated by the Ferrara–Flesch–Gethner conjecture and the List Colouring Conjecture; no resolution is given.
title: List distinguishing index conjecture for connected graphs
source_name: Jakub Kwaśny and Marcin Stawiski, “List distinguishing index of graphs”, arXiv:2306.06418 (2023).
technical_reason: All connected finite/infinite graphs and cardinal list sizes require automorphism-breaking list constructions; symmetry examples give no general bridge.

statement:
Let $P$ be a poset, and let $\mathop{}\\!\operatorname{extsat}(n,P)$ denote the minimum size of an external $P$-saturated family for the Boolean lattice ${\mathcal B}_n$, as defined in the paper. **External saturation conjecture.** For every poset $P$, there exists a constant $C_P$ independent of $n$ such that

$$
\operatorname{extsat}(n,P)\le C_P.
$$

The authors note that the dichotomy arguments for projective saturation also apply to external saturation, but no poset with unbounded external saturation number is known. This is the precise formal version of the preceding abstract-level conjecture.
title: Uniform boundedness of external saturation for posets
source_name: Dömötör Pálvölgyi and Balázs Patkós, “Projective and external saturation problem for posets”, arXiv:2306.10387 (2023).
technical_reason: External saturation depends on precise allowed embeddings. A universal bounded family for every poset is needed; no valid closure/gadget mechanism identified.

statement:
Let $p$ be a prime. Let $b_{i,j}\in\mathbb Z_p[[q]]$ be the modular forms associated with the Katz expansion of $E^\ast_{\kappa}/V(E^\ast_{\kappa})$, and let $\nu_p$ denote the $p$-adic valuation of their coefficients. Define

$$
d_p=\frac{p-1}{p(p+1)}.
$$

**Overconvergence-rate conjecture.** For all $i,j\geq 0$,

$$
\nu_p(b_{i,j})\geq d_pi-j.
$$

Equivalently, with

$$
\delta_p=\inf\left\{\frac{\nu_p(b_{i,j})+j}{i}\mathrel{\middle|}i\in\mathbb Z_{>0},\ j\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}\right\},
$$

this predicts $\delta_p\geq\frac{p-1}{p(p+1)}$. The conjecture does not assert equality; computations for low primes find values of $i$ and $j$ attaining $d_p$, in which case it would imply $\delta_p=d_p$.
title: The Eisenstein-family overconvergence-rate conjecture
source_name: Bryan Advocaat, “Computations on Overconvergence Rates Related to the Eisenstein Family”, arXiv:2306.11537 (2023).
technical_reason: All prime p and all coefficient indices require Katz expansion and valuations uniformly; small-prime equality cases cannot prove rate bound.

statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless cubic graph, and let $\mathrm{NC}(G)$ be the set of all normal $5$-colorings of $G$. Assuming the Petersen Coloring Conjecture, define $\mathrm{poor}(G)$ as the maximum number of poor edges among colorings in $\mathrm{NC}(G)$. Let $P_{10}$ be the Petersen graph, and let $P_{10}^{\Delta}$ be obtained from $P_{10}$ by truncating one vertex. **Poor-edge strengthening of the Petersen Coloring Conjecture.** If $G\ne P_{10}$, then $\mathrm{poor}(G)>0$. Moreover, if $G\ne P_{10},P_{10}^{\Delta}$, then $\mathrm{poor}(G)\geq 6$.

This proposed strengthening concerns the abundance of poor edges in normal $5$-colorings beyond the Petersen graph and its one-vertex truncation. The source attributes it to earlier work, but gives no resolution; its status is therefore open.
title: Poor-edge strengthening of the Petersen Coloring Conjecture
source_name: Jelena Sedlar and Riste Škrekovski, “Normal 5-edge-coloring of some snarks superpositioned by Flower snarks”, arXiv:2306.13340 (2024).
technical_reason: Assumes Petersen coloring and then asks for poor-edge enhancement in all nonexceptional cubic graphs. Local recoloring must preserve normality; no such general mechanism established.

statement:
Let $M$ be an **Eulerian binary matroid**, meaning a subset of $\mathbb F_2^n\setminus\{0\}$ whose elements can be decomposed into circuits. Write $c(M)$ for the minimum number of circuits in a circuit decomposition of $M$, and let $\operatorname{rank}(M)$ denote its rank. **Circuit decomposition conjecture.** For every Eulerian binary matroid $M\subseteq\mathbb F_2^n\setminus\{0\}$,

$$
c(M)\leq \left\lceil\frac{2^{\operatorname{rank}(M)}-1}{\operatorname{rank}(M)+1}\right\rceil.
$$

This would extend, up to rounding, the established bound for complete binary matroids to arbitrary Eulerian binary matroids; the conjecture remains open.
title: Circuit decomposition conjecture for Eulerian binary matroids
source_name: Bryce Frederickson and Lukas Michel, “Circuit decompositions of binary matroids”, arXiv:2306.14236 (2023).
technical_reason: Circuit decomposition bound grows with rank; small-rank enumeration cannot prove arbitrary-rank partition. No inductive split preserving the sharp ceiling found.

statement: Let $p$ be a prime. A **nice Browkin continued fraction** is the special class of Browkin continued fractions introduced by Capuano, Murru, and Terracini. **The nice-continued-fraction conjecture.** For every integer $t\geq 1$, there exists a nice Browkin continued fraction of length $t$, except when $t=1$ and $p=3$. The conjecture concerns the existence of the finite starting sequences used to construct infinite families of quadratic irrationals with periodic Browkin expansions; the source leaves it as an open problem.
title: Conjecture on nice Browkin continued fractions of every length
source_name: Giuliano Romeo, “Continued fractions in the field of p-adic numbers”, arXiv:2306.14837 (2023).
technical_reason: Nice Browkin continued-fraction conditions absent; arbitrary-length construction for all primes except stated exception needs arithmetic divisibility control, not generic periodic fractions.

statement:
Let $ll in N$ with $ll ge 2$, and let $q$ be the largest prime power with $q le ll$. For sufficiently large $t in N$, let $\falM$ be the class of matroids with no $U_{2,ll+2}$- or $M(K_{t+3})$-minor. **Crowns' extremal-function conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $n$,

$$
h_{\falM}(n)=q^t n+\fleft(\frac{q^t-1}{q-1}-tq^t\right).
$$

The preceding theorem supplies matching bounds up to the stated gap, and the authors explain that the lower bound comes from crowns and believe it is correct for large $t$ and $n$; proving that crowns are extremal remains open.
title: Crowns are extremal for matroids omitting a complete-graphic minor
source_name: Peter Nelson, Sergey Norin and Fernanda Rivera Omana, “On the density of matroids omitting a complete-graphic minor”, arXiv:2306.15061 (2023).
technical_reason: Eventual extremal growth for excluded matroid minors requires large-rank structure. Malformed macros retained; crowns lower bound alone supplies no matching upper bound.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. For vertices $u,v$ and an integer $a$, let $n_a(u,v)$ be the number of vertices whose distance difference relative to $u$ and $v$ equals $a$. Call $G$ **NT-balanced** when $n_a(u,v)=n_a(v,u)$ for every pair of vertices $u,v$ and every relevant integer $a$. Call it **ultra NT-balanced** when, for every pair $u,v$, there is an involution of the vertex set pairing vertices counted by $n_a(u,v)$ with vertices counted by $n_a(v,u)$.

**NT-balance equivalence conjecture.** Every NT-balanced graph is also ultra NT-balanced.

The paper proves that ultra NT-balanced graphs are closed under Cartesian products and uses this to construct arbitrarily large examples. Whether every NT-balanced graph admits the required involutions remains open.
title: The equivalence of NT-balanced and ultra NT-balanced graphs
source_name: Linus Tang, “Extremal Bounds on Peripherality Measures”, arXiv:2306.15702 (2023).
technical_reason: Primary v1 defines NT-balanced by N_0=0 and ultra by N_a=0 for all integers a, with strict distance inequality. Record instead imposes symmetry for every a and describes involutions. Pairing finite equal fibers only fixes the transcription, not source Conjecture 6.8.
local_proof: No new candidate proof; rejected wording diagnostics only

statement: Let $\mathcal{T}$ be an $r$-tree with maximum degree $\Delta$, where $r\geq 3$. A **toppled digraph** is a digraph associated with $\mathcal{T}$ through a choice of ordering and toppling construction. **Cycle-length conjecture.** Some toppled digraph of $\mathcal{T}$ contains cycles of length $kr$ for every integer $k$ with $1\leq k\leq\Delta$. This conjecture concerns the possible cycle structure of toppled digraphs; the preceding result shows that every directed cycle has length divisible by $r$, but the asserted existence of cycles of all multiples $r,2r,\ldots,\Delta r$ is not resolved here.
title: Cycle-length conjecture for toppled digraphs of uniform trees
source_name: Honghai Li, Li Su and Shaun Fallat, “On a relationship between the characteristic and matching polynomials of a uniform hypertree”, arXiv:2306.16247 (2023).
technical_reason: Need one toppled digraph simultaneously realizing all kr for k<=Delta; cycle divisibility and separate topplings per k do not suffice. Definitions need body recovery.

statement:
For $0<\alpha<1$, let $\rho_4(\alpha)$ be the largest real number such that, asymptotically in $N$, every sufficiently Fourier-uniform subset of $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ of density at least $\alpha$ has 4-AP density at least $\rho_4(\alpha)$. **Ruzsa's question.** For every $C>0$,

$$
\rho_4(\alpha)<\alpha^C
$$

for all sufficiently small $\alpha$. This asks whether the minimum 4-AP density tends to zero faster than every polynomial in the density. The paper notes that this remains open, with only substantially weaker upper and lower bounds known.
title: Ruzsa's question on minimum Fourier-uniform 4-AP density
source_name: Mingyang Deng, Jonathan Tidor and Yufei Zhao, “Uniform sets with few progressions via colorings”, arXiv:2307.06914 (2025).
technical_reason: For every C superpolynomial decay needs a density/uniformity construction with quantitative control; one Fourier-uniform finite witness cannot decide the limit.

statement:
For each integer $k\geq4$ and $0<\alpha<1$, let $\rho_k(\alpha)$ be the largest real number such that sufficiently $U^{k-2}$-uniform subsets of $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ of density approximately $\alpha$ have $k$-AP density at least $\rho_k(\alpha)$. **Ruzsa's extended question.** Let $k\geq4$. For every $C>0$,

$$
\rho_k(\alpha)<\alpha^C
$$

for all sufficiently small $\alpha$. The paper proves this for odd $k\geq5$ in a weaker quantitative form, while the general claim remains open for even $k$.
title: Ruzsa's question for minimum $U^{k-2}$-uniform $k$-AP density
source_name: Mingyang Deng, Jonathan Tidor and Yufei Zhao, “Uniform sets with few progressions via colorings”, arXiv:2307.06914 (2025).
technical_reason: All even k remains outside the stated odd-k result. No parameter reduction from odd to even controlling Gowers uniformity and density established.

statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a field of characteristic zero, let $f\in\mathbb{F}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and let $g$ be a factor of $f$. Write $L(h)$ for the size of the smallest arithmetic circuit computing $h$ from the variables and arbitrary constants in $\mathbb{F}$.

**Factor Conjecture.** One has

$$
L(g)\leq\operatorname{poly}(L(f)+\deg(g)).
$$

This is a central question in algebraic complexity theory. It is known for approximate complexity, and the source explains that a possible failure in the exact setting could only arise when $g$ occurs with exponentially large multiplicity.
title: The Factor Conjecture for arithmetic circuit complexity
source_name: Peter Bürgisser and Gorav Jindal, “On the Hardness of PosSLP”, arXiv:2307.08008 (2023).
technical_reason: Exact arithmetic factor complexity with potentially exponential multiplicity is the obstruction; approximate circuits or bounded-multiplicity lifting do not resolve full scope.

statement:
Let $h(n)$ denote the maximum, over complete $n$-vertex simple topological graphs, of the minimum number of crossings of an edge in a suitable noncrossing matching construction. **Short-edge crossing-number conjecture.** For every integer $n\geq 2$, 
$$
h(n)=\Theta(n^{3/2}).
$$
 This would improve the currently established bound and sharpen the quantitative understanding of short edges in complete topological graphs; the source gives no resolution of the conjecture.
title: The short-edge crossing-number conjecture
source_name: Andrew Suk, “On short edges in complete topological graphs”, arXiv:2307.08165 (2023).
technical_reason: Definition of h is source-dependent and asymptotic upper and lower bounds both needed; finite drawn configurations cannot establish n^(3/2) order.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, and let $\mathrm{sp}(G)=\mathrm{mc}(G)-m/2$ denote its surplus, where $\mathrm{mc}(G)$ is the number of edges in a largest bipartite subgraph of $G$. For a fixed graph $H$, let $\mathrm{sp}(m,H)$ be the smallest value of $\mathrm{sp}(G)$ over all $H$-free graphs $G$ with $m$ edges. **Alon–Bollobás–Krivelevich–Sudakov conjecture.** For any fixed graph $H$, there is a constant $\epsilon(H)>0$ such that

$$
\mathrm{sp}(m,H)=\Omega(m^{3/4+\epsilon(H)}).
$$

The conjecture predicts a uniform improvement over the general $\Omega(\sqrt m)$ surplus bound for every fixed forbidden graph $H$. It remains open; the best known lower bounds establish weaker exponents for particular families of $H$.
title: Alon–Bollobás–Krivelevich–Sudakov surplus conjecture for H-free graphs
source_name: Jinghua Deng, Jianfeng Hou, Siwei Lin and Qinghou Zeng, “MaxCut in graphs with sparse neighborhoods”, arXiv:2307.09309 (2023).
technical_reason: Uniform exponent improvement for every fixed forbidden H requires large-scale surplus arguments; degenerate forbidden-graph conventions are no substantive counterexample.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, and let $\mathrm{sp}(G)=\mathrm{mc}(G)-m/2$ denote its surplus, where $\mathrm{mc}(G)$ is the number of edges in a largest bipartite subgraph of $G$. For a fixed graph $H$, let $\mathrm{sp}(m,H)$ be the smallest value of $\mathrm{sp}(G)$ over all $H$-free graphs $G$ with $m$ edges. **Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov conjecture.** For any fixed graph $H$, there is a constant $c(H)>0$ such that

$$
\mathrm{sp}(m,H)=\Theta(m^{c(H)}).
$$

This conjecture seeks the precise order of the surplus for every fixed forbidden graph, strengthening the problem of obtaining a universal lower-bound exponent. The paper presents it as a more difficult conjecture and does not report a resolution.
title: Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov surplus order-of-magnitude conjecture
source_name: Jinghua Deng, Jianfeng Hou, Siwei Lin and Qinghou Zeng, “MaxCut in graphs with sparse neighborhoods”, arXiv:2307.09309 (2023).
technical_reason: Pure-power Theta asymptotics excludes logarithmic corrections and asks every H; lower-bound progress alone cannot determine exponent or matching upper bound.

statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $m$ edges, and let $\mathrm{sp}(G)=\mathrm{mc}(G)-m/2$ denote its surplus, where $\mathrm{mc}(G)$ is the number of edges in a largest bipartite subgraph of $G$. For integers $t\ge s\ge2$, let $K_{s,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph with parts of sizes $s$ and $t$, and let $\mathrm{sp}(m,K_{s,t})$ be the smallest surplus among all $K_{s,t}$-free graphs with $m$ edges. **Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov conjecture.** For all $t\ge s\ge2$ and all $m$,

$$
\mathrm{sp}(m,K_{s,t})=\Omega\left(m^{\frac34+\frac{1}{8s-4}}\right).
$$

This is a special case of the general surplus conjecture for forbidden graphs. The source presents it as open and discusses bounds for this family.
title: Alon–Krivelevich–Sudakov conjecture for K_{s,t}-free graphs
source_name: Jinghua Deng, Jianfeng Hou, Siwei Lin and Qinghou Zeng, “MaxCut in graphs with sparse neighborhoods”, arXiv:2307.09309 (2023).
technical_reason: All s,t needs exponent 3/4+1/(8s-4), not selected complete bipartite cases; no short transfer from neighborhood sparsity with sharp exponent verified.

statement:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ be a hypergraph family, and let $m_\mathcal{H}(k)$ denote the minimum number of vertices needed to guarantee a polychromatic $k$-coloring in the relevant hypergraphs of $\mathcal{H}$. **Linear polychromatic coloring conjecture.** If

$$
m_\mathcal{H}(2)<\infty
$$

for a hypergraph family $\mathcal{H}$, then

$$
m_\mathcal{H}(k)=O(k).
$$

The conjecture asserts that finiteness of the two-color threshold forces a linear bound for every number of colors. The surrounding discussion relates this question to shallow hitting sets and the linear bound supplied by the preceding lemma; no resolution is given here.
title: The linear polychromatic coloring conjecture for hypergraph families
source_name: Balázs Bursics, Bence Csonka and Luca Szepessy, “Hitting sets and colorings of hypergraphs”, arXiv:2307.12154 (2026).
technical_reason: Arbitrary family H requires precise closure assumptions. Iterated two-colorability by itself may lose linear dependence; no shallow-hitting-set theorem derived for full scope.

statement:
For each positive integer $m$, let $\ell_m$ be the minimum mean value of the representation function over subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_m$ that represent every residue, and let $\mathcal{K}_m$ be the minimum cardinality of a subset $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_m$ satisfying $1\leq\sigma_A(n)\leq R_m$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}_m$.

**Attainment conjecture.** For all sufficiently large $m$,

$$
\mathcal{K}_m^2=m\ell_m.
$$

The source motivates this by suggesting that $\ell_m$ is eventually attained by a set in $\mathcal{H}^*_m$, but provides no proof or resolution.
title: Conjecture on attainment of the minimal mean representation count
source_name: Yuchen Ding and Lilu Zhao, “A new upper bound on Ruzsa's number on the Erdős-Turán conjecture”, arXiv:2307.12311 (2023).
technical_reason: All sufficiently large moduli require simultaneous mean optimum and bounded representation optimum; finite subset enumeration would be only instances and R_m definitions unverified.

statement:
A **finite two-dimensional ruleset** is a finite set of subtraction moves on two-dimensional lattice positions. Such a ruleset is **eventually periodic** when its outcomes are eventually periodic on every relevant rational-slope lattice line, with the corresponding periods and thresholds uniformly bounded as specified in the paper.

**Non-eventual-periodicity conjecture.** Not all finite two-dimensional rulesets are eventually periodic.

This claim distinguishes two-dimensional outcome segmentation from eventual periodicity and asserts that finite rulesets can exhibit genuinely non-eventually-periodic behavior. It appears in the paper’s discussion of open questions, and the source gives no resolution status.
title: Non-eventual-periodicity conjecture for finite two-dimensional subtraction
source_name: Urban Larsson, Indrajit Saha and Makoto Yokoo, “Subtraction games in more than one dimension”, arXiv:2307.12458 (2024).
technical_reason: A finite move set with proved nonperiodic rational-line outcomes could be a certificate, but no explicit set plus unbounded nonperiodicity invariant identified. Accepted randomized odd-subtraction result concerns a different mechanism and supplies no bridge.

statement:
Let $q\geq 2$ and $n\geq 3$. Let $\mathcal{M}_{q,n}$ denote the family of maximum non-overlapping codes of length $n$, and for a code $C\in\mathcal{M}_{q,n}$ write

$$
C=\bigcup_{i<n}\left(L_iR_{n-i}\right),
$$

where $L_i$ and $R_i$ are the corresponding left and right component sets. **Structural conjecture.** For every $q\geq 2$ and $n\geq 3$, there exists a maximum non-overlapping code $C\in\mathcal{M}_{q,n}$ satisfying

$$
R_i=\emptyset\quad\text{for every }i>\frac{n}{q+1}+1.
$$

The conjecture describes a common structural property of optimal solutions to the reduced optimization problem and remains unresolved according to the supplied context.
title: Conjecture on the structure of maximum non-overlapping codes
source_name: Lidija Stanovnik, Miha Moškon and Miha Mraz, “In search of maximum non-overlapping codes”, arXiv:2307.12593 (2024).
technical_reason: Every q,n structural optimum would require exhaustive optimality or a transformation preserving code size and moving high-index R_i to zero. No such transformation established.

statement:
Let $a(G)$ be the annihilation number, $\alpha(G)$ the independence number, and $\mu(G)$ the matching number of a bipartite graph $G$. The graph is called **extremal** when equality holds in the bipartite bound

$$
a(G)-\alpha(G)=2+\mu(G)-2\sqrt{1+\mu(G)}.
$$

**Minimum-order conjecture.** The minimum number of vertices of an extremal bipartite graph is $16$.

The claim identifies the smallest order at which equality in the paper's sharp bipartite inequality can occur. Its resolution is not indicated in the supplied material, so it remains open in this record.
title: Minimum order of an extremal bipartite graph
source_name: Ohr Kadrawi and Vadim E. Levit, “Inequalities Connecting the Annihilation and Independence Numbers”, arXiv:2308.01685 (2023).
technical_reason: Primary v1 Conjecture 5.3 checked along with Theorems 3.2-3.4. mu=0 edgeless equality trivially defeats unrestricted wording, so no credit. Substantive positive-edge case requires lower-order exclusion; source p>=3 family starts at 16 but does not establish minimality. No bounded exhaustive graph classification performed.
local_proof: No new candidate proof; rejected wording diagnostics only

statement: For a finite set of points in the plane, consider every line determined by at least two points of the set, and compare the numbers of points on its two sides. **Stretchable-configuration conjecture.** There exists an unbounded function $f:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every natural number $n$, there is a set of $n$ points for which the numbers of points on either side of each line determined by the set differ by at least $f(n)$. The paper's construction establishes the analogous phenomenon for pseudoline arrangements, while the stretchability of such configurations remains open; the conjecture proposes that configurations realizable by lines can also exhibit unbounded imbalance.
title: Conjectured unbounded imbalance for stretchable point configurations
source_name: David Conlon and Jeck Lim, “Everywhere unbalanced configurations”, arXiv:2308.02466 (2025).
technical_reason: Unbounded imbalance for stretchable configurations is not disproved by known imbalance-two examples. Corpus refuted metadata is logically unrelated; no uniform geometric construction found.

statement:
Let $G$ be a planar triangulation on $n$ vertices, meaning a plane graph in which every face is bounded by a triangle, and let $\iota(G)$ denote its independent domination number, the minimum cardinality of an independent dominating set of $G$. **Goddard–Henning's conjecture.** For every planar triangulation $G$ on $n$ vertices, we have

$$
\iota(G) \leq n/3.
$$

The conjecture arises from the question of whether every planar triangulation has three disjoint independent dominating sets; this would imply the stated bound. The paper presents it as a conjecture, and its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
title: Goddard–Henning independent domination conjecture for planar triangulations
source_name: Fábio Botler, Cristina G. Fernandes and Juan Gutiérrez, “Independent dominating sets in planar triangulations”, arXiv:2308.02754 (2023).
technical_reason: Every planar triangulation needs n/3 independent domination, not just a small dominating set or three independent color classes lacking domination. No local reduction preserving the sharp ratio established.
